clue.text: When you're in it, you wish you were out of it, and it's not a funny mix-up!

definitions.text: When you're in it, you wish you were out of it

parts.note: something that is not funny is serious
a mix-up, a confused scrap or fracas, is trouble

explanation.surface: A wry remark about a predicament that nobody finds amusing to be caught in.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across two lights: the first word in 1 and the second in 5.
explanation.definitionFit: Serious trouble is a grave predicament, the kind of situation anyone caught up in it longs to escape.

clue.text: There's a reminder of injury on those muscles some want to be flat, like the images of the Egyptians.

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece placed on another sits above it

parts.note: a scar is the mark a wound leaves behind

parts.words: those muscles some want to be flat
parts.note: ABS, the abdominal muscles, which many want as a flat stomach

explanation.surface: Someone with an old wound on a toned belly, compared to ancient Egyptian art.
explanation.walkthrough: Abs is short for abdominal muscles; 'on' puts SCAR above ABS in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarabs are carved beetle amulets, a familiar emblem of ancient Egyptian religion and art.

clue.text: You have to come out before you can make one.

definitions.text: You have to come out before you can make one.

parts.words: You have to come out before you can make one
parts.note: going back in is only possible after first leaving, so the clue describes coming back in

explanation.surface: Sounds like advice about a debutante or a comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come out' hints at a debut, but the point is simpler: you can only go back in somewhere you have already left.
explanation.definitionFit: A reentry is the act of entering again, which presupposes an earlier exit.

clue.text: They blow in the woods, like other reeds.

definitions.text: They blow in the woods, like other reeds.

parts.words: They blow in the woods, like other reeds
parts.note: the woods here are the woodwind section, and these double-reed instruments are blown

explanation.surface: Pictures reeds swaying in the breeze in a forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woods' is the orchestra's woodwind section, not a forest, and the reeds are instruments rather than plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Oboes are double-reed woodwind instruments played by blowing.

clue.text: The sort of phrases that often guide people.

indicators.note: to sort something is to rearrange it, so the letters of phrases are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Seems to describe the kind of wording found on signposts or in instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The sort of phrases' looks like a description; 'sort' is the rearranging signal. The words 'that often guide' describe these people.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherpas are a Himalayan people famous for guiding climbers on Everest and other peaks.

clue.text: See 1
A sailor that a famous Lily went after, with scales of silver.

indicators.note: the second piece comes after the first in the answer

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
Lily Pons, the celebrated French-American coloratura soprano

explanation.surface: A seaman pursued by a famous woman named Lily, with a silvery touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarpons are big game fish whose bodies are covered in large, gleaming silvery scales.

clue.text: "Guts!"–that sounds awful!

indicators.note: says the answer is pronounced like the word awful

parts.note: the word heard

explanation.surface: Someone recoiling in disgust at a mention of entrails.
explanation.definitionFit: Offal is the entrails and organs of a butchered animal, its innards.

clue.text: A bunch of hay, not quite full of this, and somewhat threatening.

parts.note: a bale is a bound bundle of hay

indicators.note: says the word full falls just short, losing its final letter

parts.note: the word as written

explanation.surface: A haystack only partly full, with an ominous air about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Baleful means menacing or harmful in intent, a stronger relative of the gloss given.

clue.text: What one often does to check the last part, with all but Dobbin's head.

definitions.text: What one often does to check

parts.note: the end is the last part of anything

indicators.note: says everything is kept except one piece, named by the next indicator
the head of a word is its first letter, which is what goes

parts.note: Dobbin is a traditional name for a farm horse

explanation.surface: Reads like advice to review the ending, with a horse somehow involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All but' with 'head' drops the first letter of HORSE, leaving ORSE; Dobbin is a stock name for a farm horse. 'Check' is a bank cheque: you endorse one by signing its back.
explanation.definitionFit: Endorsing a check means signing it on the back so that it can be cashed or deposited.

clue.text: Possibly one name for a flower in the buttercup family.

definitions.text: a flower in the buttercup family

indicators.note: says the letters of one name may be arranged in another way

explanation.surface: Suggests a candidate name for a bloom related to buttercups.
explanation.definitionFit: Anemones, or windflowers, belong to the Ranunculaceae, the botanical family of buttercups.

clue.text: What some frown on as apparel in return–as the runaway did–when feathers get so mixed up.

definitions.text: when feathers get so mixed up

indicators.note: says this piece is turned back to front

parts.words: What some frown on as apparel
parts.note: fur, worn as clothing, draws disapproval from many
a runaway fled

explanation.surface: A tangled scene of disapproved clothing, a fugitive, and messy plumage.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruffled describes feathers disordered and standing up, as on an agitated bird.

clue.text: Throws something in the pot, possibly.

definitions.text: Throws something in the pot, possibly.

parts.words: Throws something in the pot, possibly
parts.note: in poker each player puts a stake into the pot before the deal

explanation.surface: Could be a cook tossing ingredients into a stewpot.
explanation.walkthrough: The pot is the poker kitty, not a cooking vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To ante is to put in a stake before cards are dealt in poker.

clue.text: Produce by multiplication, according to the figures of those against birth control.

parts.note: pro-life campaigners, who oppose abortion
a rate is a figure, such as a birth rate

explanation.surface: Reproduction framed by the statistics of anti-contraception campaigners.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is split over three lights: 12, 13 and 26 across.
explanation.definitionFit: To proliferate is to increase rapidly in number, as cells do by repeated division.

clue.text: See 12
The way the Brits throw things on the loch, typified by violets.

parts.words: The way the Brits throw things
parts.note: in British English to shy something is to fling it, as at a coconut shy
Loch Ness, the Scottish lake famous for its monster

explanation.surface: A British throwing style on a Scottish lake, somehow linked with violets.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the quality typified, from 'shrinking violet', a timid person. A coconut shy is a British fairground stall where you throw balls at coconuts.
explanation.definitionFit: A bashful person is called a shrinking violet, so this timid quality is what violets stand for.

clue.text: See 17
Is evil less likely to show it in Spain?

indicators.note: says the answer is on view within the run of words Is evil less

parts.note: the answer sits inside these words: iS EVIL LEss

explanation.surface: Wonders whether wickedness is less visible on Spanish soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Likely to show it' points to the answer sitting in plain view across 'Is evil less'. The definition is loose: a city located in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Seville is the Andalusian capital, a major city of southern Spain.

clue.text: Five letters, and sometimes W and Y, with what the groom does when taking overhead transportation.

definitions.text: Five letters, and sometimes W and Y

indicators.note: one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: at a wedding the groom vows
an el is an American elevated railway

explanation.surface: Mixes the alphabet with a wedding and an elevated train ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When taking' signals one piece swallowing another. The El is the elevated railway of Chicago or old New York, hence 'overhead transportation'. The answer is split over 17 and 15 down.
explanation.definitionFit: A, E, I, O and U are vowels, with W and Y sometimes counted among them.

clue.text: What such meat comes from sounds dear, with outrageous noise following 5, to a point.

definitions.text: What such meat comes from sounds dear

indicators.note: the next piece comes after the first

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

indicators.note: the letters of noise are wildly disordered

parts.note: N, north, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A puzzling mix of costly meat, uproar and a cross-reference to clue 5.
explanation.walkthrough: The 5 looks like a cross-reference but is the Roman numeral V; 'outrageous' rearranges the noise to ENISO and 'following' places it after V. The definition is cryptic: meat from what sounds like 'dear'.
explanation.definitionFit: Venison is deer meat, and a deer is an animal whose name is pronounced the same as dear.

clue.text: Blue in a lover's verse, though of a slightly different color, with one of the strings set improperly.

definitions.text: Blue in a lover's verse, though of a slightly different color

parts.note: the viol is a stringed instrument

indicators.note: the letters of set are arranged wrongly

explanation.surface: Muses on a love poem whose colours do not quite match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Improperly' turns SET into ETS. The lover's verse is 'Roses are red, violets are blue', though the flowers are really purple.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyme calls violets blue, while the flowers are actually purplish.

clue.text: Describing those who are frequent travelers?

definitions.text: Describing those who are frequent travelers?

parts.words: Describing those who are frequent travelers
parts.note: an adjective for people always on the move, wandering from place to place

explanation.surface: Sounds like a term for business people with air miles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frequent travelers' suggests flyers with loyalty cards; it means wandering peoples.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomadic describes peoples who wander without a fixed home, moving with herds or seasons.

clue.text: Subtle distinctions when the sun comes up around the swaying cane.

indicators.note: the turned word sun goes around the rest
in a down answer, rising means the word sun is read from bottom to top
the letters of cane are unsettled and rearranged

explanation.surface: A sunrise over a field of canes bending in the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuances are fine shades of meaning or difference.

clue.text: Baffles most of the unsightly things.

indicators.note: says the word the loses its final letter

parts.note: warts are unsightly growths on the skin

explanation.surface: Someone puzzled by blemishes.
explanation.definitionFit: To thwart someone is to frustrate or foil them, which is what baffles means as a verb.

clue.text: Aren't women allowed to hold property here?

definitions.text: Aren't women allowed to hold property here?

parts.words: Aren't women allowed to hold property here
parts.note: the joke is a place whose name says it belongs to men only

explanation.surface: A pointed question about women's property rights somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is split over two lights, 21 down and 24 across. The Isle of Man is a self-governing island in the Irish Sea; its name sounds like male ownership.
explanation.definitionFit: The island's name reads as if it were possessed by man, joking that women own nothing there.

clue.text: Polish the symbol of what implied a decisive crossing.

parts.note: to rub is to polish
an icon is a symbol or emblem

explanation.surface: Instructions for shining up an emblem of a historic river crossing.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar's crossing of the river Rubicon committed him to civil war, giving the idiom of a point of no return.

clue.text: Material didn't stand around part of the fork.

indicators.note: the first word goes around the other

parts.note: someone who didn't stand sat
a tine is a prong of a fork

explanation.surface: Fabric that stayed seated around a fork prong.
explanation.definitionFit: Satinet is a thin imitation satin cloth, often of cotton and wool.

clue.text: See 21 down
So-called way you can get to amend the answer.

indicators.note: says the letters of amend can be rearranged to reach the answer

explanation.surface: A so-called method for correcting an answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Way you can get to' tells you to rearrange AMEND; 'the answer' at the end only points to what the rearranged letters give.
explanation.definitionFit: Named means called or designated by a particular name, just as so-called does.

clue.text: See 12
One who is seen coming out with it as an IOU recording.

parts.words: One who is seen coming out
parts.note: a deb, a debutante, is a young woman making her coming out in society

explanation.surface: A debutante's coming-out party turned into a ledger entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A debit is an accounting entry recording a sum owed, like the debt an IOU acknowledges.

clue.text: Dialectically dared dust around Robespierre's head.

indicators.note: the word dust goes around the other piece
the head of a name is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of Robespierre

explanation.surface: Revolutionary history: someone bold enough to throw dust on Robespierre's head.
explanation.definitionFit: Durst is an archaic and dialect past tense of dare.

clue.text: Confined to a particular place, at last the little rodents appear back to front.

parts.note: at last is at the end

indicators.note: the back letter of the word is moved round to the front

parts.note: mice are little rodents

explanation.surface: Mice finally scurrying backwards in some local setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appear back to front' is not a full reversal: only the back letter of MICE moves to the front, making EMIC.
explanation.definitionFit: An endemic disease or species is native to, and restricted to, a certain region.

clue.text: One might be found in a nomadic tribe, but race in endless sand.

definitions.text: One might be found in a nomadic tribe

indicators.note: says the word race goes inside the other piece
the word sand loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A desert tribesman racing across shifting sand.
explanation.definitionFit: Saracen was the old name for the desert Arabs, nomadic peoples of the Syrian-Arabian deserts.

clue.text: Acts rebellious, with a short time as they say, to scatter the seed.

parts.note: sec is short for second, a brief moment

indicators.note: marks the next words as heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to scatter seed is to seed, so seeds is the word heard

explanation.surface: Rebels sowing seed in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As they say' means the sowing word is heard, not spelt: the written ending is EDES, because when spoken the hard C of the short time runs straight into the S sound that opens seeds.
explanation.definitionFit: To secede is to withdraw formally from a union or federation, a rebellious act.

clue.text: No longer with us, with the text needing amending about what follows the company name, perhaps.

indicators.note: the reworked word goes around the other piece
says the letters of text are to be put right in a new order

parts.words: what follows the company name, perhaps
parts.note: Inc., short for incorporated, follows many American company names

explanation.surface: A defunct firm whose paperwork needs correcting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needing amending' turns TEXT into EXTT, which goes about INC.
explanation.definitionFit: Extinct describes a species or thing that has died out and exists no more.
